newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Raul Salinas cleared of fraud charges.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Raul Salinas cleared of fraud charges.

text.p: Raul Salinas, the jailed brother of ex-Mexican president Carlos Salinas, has won the first round of a legal battle with the government after a judge cleared him of tax fraud charges.

Federal appeals court Judge Raul Melgoza Figueroa ordered the charges dropped late on Tuesday after finding there was too little evidence to convict Salinas, who remained in a maximum-security prison in Mexico City on a host of other charges including murder.

Salinas was arrested in early 1995 on charges he plotted the 1994 assasination of top ruling party official Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu. He was later also charged with tax fraud, illicit enrichment and falsification of documents, becoming to many Mexicans a symbol of corruption in his brothers' 1988-1994 term.
The Mexican finance ministry said in a statement late on Tuesday it would continue to investigate Raul Salinas' finances and could press additional charges of tax evasion.

But with the murder probe against him snagged in scandal and suffering from what his lawyers say is a lack of hard evidence, the ruling could mark a turning point in the legal fortunes of Raul Salinas, supporters said.

"This is an important victory. These are the first charges dropped against Mr. Salinas and an important first step (in clearing him of other charges)," Juan Velasquez, one of Salinas' lawyers, told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Velasquez, who is not representing Salinas on the murder charge, said he believed his client would also be cleared of corruption charges for lack of evidence.

The murder case against Raul Salinas suffered a big blow recently after officials bungled an investigation into a body found on Salinas' ranch in late 1996 -- a body that was supposed to hold the key to the murder mystery.

At the time of the body's discovery, officials suggested it belonged to a congressman accused of helping Raul Salinas plot the Ruiz Massieu murder but who went missing shortly after. Officials believe Raul may have double-crossed his partner in crime.
But the body was not that of congressman Manuel Munoz Rocha. It was planted intentionally by a reputed witch who was on the payroll of former Attorney General Antonio Lozano Gracia.

Lozano Gracia, a member of the opposition PAN party who was fired in December, on Tuesday denied insinuations by the PRI that he had planted the body to help his case against Raul and claimed he was the victim of a political lynching.

Lozano admitted he authorised payments to the witch, but suggested that was more a mistake than an attempt to pervert justice. He urged investigators to follow up testimony from the witch that Raul Salinas had blackmailed her into burying the body to derail the probe against him.
Lozano was the only member of the opposition ever to hold a cabinet post.
